messages.author: 06199470668a2843
messages.subject: Disappearing factor levels of covariates
parts:
Hello everyone,

I am currently running models (on Distance 6.01 Beta) that include
multiple factor covariates, of 3-10 levels each. I have noticed that in
all listings the Detection Fct/Global/Parameter Estimates screen, the las=
t
level of each factor covariate seems to be missing. E.g., using the
10-level covariate "CIRCUIT", the 3-level covariate "OBSERVER" and the
nonfactor covariate "WIND", the following output is given:

Model
Hazard Rate key, k(y) =3D 1 - Exp(-(y/s)**-A(2))
Hermite polynomial adjustments of order(s) : 4

s =3D A(1) * Exp(fcn(A(3)) + fcn(A(4)) + fcn(A(5)) + fcn(A(6)) +
fcn(A(7)) + fcn(A(8)) + fcn(A(9)) + fcn(A(10)) + fcn(A(11)) +
fcn(A(12)) + fcn(A(13)) + fcn(A(14)))
Parameter A(1) is the intercept of the scale parameter s.
Parameter A(2) is the power parameter.
Parameter A(3) is the coefficient of level 1 of factor covariate CIRCU=
IT.
Parameter A(4) is the coefficient of level 10 of factor covariate CIRC=
UIT.
Parameter A(5) is the coefficient of level 2 of factor covariate CIRCU=
IT.
Parameter A(6) is the coefficient of level 3 of factor covariate CIRCU=
IT.
Parameter A(7) is the coefficient of level 4 of factor covariate CIRCU=
IT.
Parameter A(8) is the coefficient of level 5 of factor covariate CIRCU=
IT.
Parameter A(9) is the coefficient of level 6 of factor covariate CIRCU=
IT.
Parameter A(10) is the coefficient of level 7 of factor covariate CIRC=
UIT.
Parameter A(11) is the coefficient of level 8 of factor covariate CIRC=
UIT.
Parameter A(12) is the coefficient of covariate WIND.
Parameter A(13) is the coefficient of level FLORIAN of factor covariat=
e
OBSERVER.
Parameter A(14) is the coefficient of level FLORIAN & OTHER of factor
covariate OBSERVER.
Parameter A(15) is the coefficient of the adjustment term of order 4.

Missing from this would be level 9 (last in the numerical sequence) of
CIRCUIT, and level OTHER of OBSERVER. It would be of particular interest
to me to have all the levels present in the sampling correlation table.

Plots for combinations involving the missing covariate levels are
provided, though, so they don't seem to be ignored, just not tabulated?

Are the missing levels used as a reference level for the other levels, an=
d
therefore omitted? If so, is there a reason that the LAST level is used b=
y
default instead of the first one?

I hope that someone can shed some light on this :)
cheers!
florian

messages.author: 5900eadecec2d82d
messages.subject: Re: Disappearing factor levels of covariates
parts:
Florian,

The last factor corresponds with the intercept (parameter A(1)) - i.e.,
it is the reference level, as you suspected. This is explained in the
online manual -- type Factor in the index, and look at the topic listed
under "Factor and Non-factor covariates in MCDS". RTFM!

There are many ways to turn factor levels into a design matrix, and our
choice in Distance to use the last one as a "reference" is arbitrary.

Cheers,

- len
